title: a native pin whose argument does not resolve to a function declared in this project is rejected: an assertion that cannot be checked is not an assertion
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin' (Locked): 'A native pin MUST be a checked assertion over the complete transitive graph.' docs/DECISIONS.md, 'TypeScript and native classification' (Locked): 'A function explicitly pinned as native is a checked assertion. It is a compile error if any transitive operation or provider requires TypeScript; diagnostics must show the dependency path.' Both sentences presuppose a subject: there is no transitive graph to check and no dependency path to show without one, so a pin whose subject the compiler cannot identify has to be refused rather than ignored. THIS CODE IS THE GATE ON THE WHOLE AREA and until now it was unprobed: of the twenty-six other cases in `21-native-pin`, twenty-five hand `native(...)` a well-formed reference and the twenty-sixth is this rule's other branch (`a-pin-given-two-arguments-is-rejected`), so before these two nothing pinned what happens when the assertion itself is uncheckable. It was one of the codes that both implementations spell and no case probed — the set COVERAGE.md calls strictly worse than the reference-only set, because a shared rule nobody probes produces no signal in either direction if either implementation loses it. The declared position is the ARGUMENT, not the call: the reference reports the unresolvable-subject branch on the node it could not resolve (poc/src/targets/classify.ts, `collectNativePins`), and the fork agrees at 9:8. The rule has a second branch — the wrong number of arguments, reported at the CALL — which is pinned separately by 21-native-pin/a-pin-given-two-arguments-is-rejected, because one case per branch is what stops a backend from owning half of a code. No `messageContains` is declared. The two backends legitimately word this diagnostic differently — measured on SMITHERS1503, where the reference says "only as an expression statement or direct return" and the fork says "only as an expression statement or a direct return" — and conformance/README.md reserves `messageContains` for rules whose PAYLOAD is the promise, which here it is not: the code and the authored position are the whole contract, and a fragment of the sentence around them would be a wording assertion wearing a contract's clothes. Both backends refuse it today, so this case pins current behaviour on both rather than reproducing a live one-sided defect.
